sentences.text: Pahasapasaurus gillettei shows elongated epipodial bones—the fore- and hind-limb elements between the upper limb bones and the flippers—and a distinctive palate bone structure.
The species was announced in 2025 and the final article is scheduled for publication in 2026.
Its type locality is the Tropic Shale of Utah, United States.
Pahasapasaurus gillettei was described by Schmeisser and McKean.
It belongs to the polycotylid plesiosaurs, a group of short-necked marine reptiles.
The genus Pahasapasaurus was erected by Schumacher in 2007.
Pahasapasaurus gillettei lived during the Turonian stage of the Late Cretaceous.
Its fossils are found in Late Cretaceous rocks of the United States.
The Paleobiology Database currently contains no entry for Pahasapasaurus gillettei, indicating that its broader scientific record is still limited.
